device_info: ROCm RX 7900 XTX (WSL2, ROCm 7.2.4) for generation, capture and the teacher; CPU (Ryzen 9 9900X, WSL2) Backend::Vector for training; f32 compute, BF16 weights
note: Book 3, the Wait experiment: can training the last layer's FFN (layer 23) reproduce the hand edit of volume 1 ch5 (examples/weight-space-programming.json: one direction subtracted from 64 columns of mlp.down_proj in layers 15 and 19, found by the original authors with forward passes only, no gradients), which lets Qwen3.5-0.8B close its thinking block and cuts Wait loops? All generation is greedy thinking on ROCm, max 2,000 new tokens (tools/thinking_survey.py; rocm-chat --thinking). closed: the reply emitted </think> (ID 248069); count_Wait: occurrences of 'Wait' in the text; short loop: at least 95% of the last 200 IDs repeat with one period <= 64. Teacher data: the edited model on the 60 new prompts of examples/thinking-loop-train-prompts.txt closes 39 (base 12); those 39 replies (thinking + </think> + answer, tools/thinking_pairs.py) are the training pairs, 36,023 tokens, 35,220 scored positions. The layer-23 inputs come from the base model on the GPU (train-text --gpu rocm, checked against the CPU capture: max abs diff 2.4e-5 after the mixer, 1.1e-4 after the norm); training is on the CPU, Adam, 200 steps of 1,024 sampled positions (--sample 1024, seed 0). CE runs learn the text's next ID; KL runs (--teacher-edit, added on top of source_commit in the commit that records this file) learn the edited model's top 32 + other at every position, computed by prefilling each pair on the GPU with the edit applied and running the frozen layer 23 and head on the CPU; the teacher's top-1 is the text's ID at 0.9993 of the positions. Loss and top-1 in training.before/after are always of the text's IDs, so a KL run's CE on the text can rise (0.240 -> 0.264) while its top-1 rises (0.970 -> 0.982). Held out = the 20 ch5 prompts (examples/thinking-loop-prompts.txt), none trained on; base and edit6 reproduce the ch5 counts (3/708, 15/316). Result 1: CE does not carry the edit. On the held-out 20 the CE runs close 5-6 (base 3, edit 15) and keep 10-13 short loops; even on the 60 training prompts they close 15 against the teacher's 39. The base already picks the text's ID at 97% of positions; the decisions (another Wait or </think>) sit in the other 3%. Result 2: KL carries most of it. The full FFN at lr 3e-6 closes 12 of the held-out 20 with 376 Wait and 5 short loops (edit 15/316/2); the answers of the closed ones are correct. Prompts 6, 8, 16 and 17, which the edit also leaves open, stay open; prompt 18, open under the edit, closes. LoRA rank 8 (110,592 parameters) closes 10, 521 Wait, 8 loops. Contrast with cpu-prefecture-capitals-topk.json, where soft labels changed nothing: there the teacher was sharp (mean entropy 0.07 nats); here the targets of interest are the positions where the edited model's distribution differs from the base's. Single runs, one seed; the KL runs were not evaluated on the 60 training prompts. Seeds (added 2026-11-23): the KL full-FFN run repeated with --sample-seed 1 and 2 (only the draw of the 1,024 positions per step differs; the start is the base FFN): closed 13 / 363 Wait / 5 short loops and 11 / 477 / 6, against 12 / 376 / 5 at seed 0. So the layer-23 KL result is 11-13 closed; Wait varies more (363-477). Layers 15/19 (rocm-thinking-wait-stack.json, one seed each): KL 10, CE 12 closed; neither is clearly better or worse than layer 23 at this spread.
